# Statistic

A stat tile: a label, a value, its change compared with an earlier period, and an optional trend line. It has
no background or padding of its own: place it in a Panel, and put several of them in a Grid to form a KPI row.

**Interaction**: not interactive. The value is semibold with proportional figures. The change always has an
arrow and a sign, and screen readers read it as a sentence, such as "Up 12.5%, vs last month". While loading,
a skeleton takes the place of the value and appears after 200 ms, so fast loads do not flash; the size does
not change when the data arrives.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: KPI rows at the top of dashboards, key numbers of a project or a period, figures next to a chart

## Import

```ts
import { Statistic } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

### Basic usage

A label, a value, its change compared with an earlier period and a trend of the last 12 periods. The tile has
no background of its own: place it in a Panel.

```tsx
import { Panel, Statistic } from 'vellum-ui'

const signups = [312, 298, 341, 356, 330, 372, 389, 401, 377, 420, 436, 458]

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Panel>
      <Statistic
        label="Weekly sign-ups"
        value={458}
        delta={{ value: 0.05, period: 'vs last week' }}
        trend={signups}
      />
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

### KPI row

Put several tiles in a Grid. Large values are compact (12.9K); `prefix` and `suffix` add a currency or a unit.
When a lower value is better, set `goodWhen: 'down'`: a decrease is then shown in the success color.

```tsx
import { Grid, Panel, Statistic } from 'vellum-ui'

export function KpiRow() {
  return (
    <Grid columns={4}>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Active users"
          value={12_894}
          delta={{ value: 0.125, period: 'vs last month' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Revenue"
          value={48_210}
          prefix="$"
          delta={{ value: -0.032, period: 'vs last month' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Error rate"
          value={0.0042}
          format="percent"
          delta={{ value: -0.18, period: 'vs last week', goodWhen: 'down' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Median response time"
          value={182}
          suffix="ms"
          delta={{ value: 0.06, period: 'vs last week', goodWhen: 'down' }}
        />
      </Panel>
    </Grid>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Changes and sizes

`goodWhen: 'none'` keeps the change in the secondary text color when neither direction is better; no change
shows a flat arrow. An absolute change uses its own `format`. `size="lg"` is for the main figure of an area.

```tsx
import { Grid, Panel, Statistic } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Grid>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Open tickets"
          value={64}
          delta={{ value: 0.08, period: 'vs yesterday', goodWhen: 'none' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Uptime"
          value={0.998}
          format="percent"
          delta={{ value: 0, period: 'vs last month' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Orders shipped"
          value={1_284}
          delta={{ value: 36, format: 'number', period: 'vs yesterday' }}
        />
      </Panel>
      <Panel>
        <Statistic
          label="Storage used"
          value={3.6}
          suffix="TB"
          size="lg"
          delta={{ value: 0.02, period: 'vs last month', goodWhen: 'none' }}
        />
      </Panel>
    </Grid>
  )
}
```

## States

### Loading and no data

While `loading`, skeletons take the place of the value, the change and the trend, and appear after 200 ms; the
tile keeps its size when the data arrives. A `null` value shows a dash.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Grid, Inline, Panel, Stack, Statistic, Switch, Text } from 'vellum-ui'

const signups = [312, 298, 341, 356, 330, 372, 389, 401, 377, 420, 436, 458]

export function States() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <Inline gap={2} align="center">
        <Switch checked={loading} onChange={setLoading} aria-label="Loading" />
        <Text size="sm">Loading</Text>
      </Inline>
      <Grid>
        <Panel>
          <Statistic
            label="Weekly sign-ups"
            value={458}
            delta={{ value: 0.05, period: 'vs last week' }}
            trend={signups}
            loading={loading}
          />
        </Panel>
        <Panel>
          <Statistic label="Refunds" value={null} />
        </Panel>
      </Grid>
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | What the number is, in sentence case and without a trailing colon, such as "Monthly revenue". | — | Yes |
| `value` | `number \| null` | The value. `null` shows a dash (no data). | — | Yes |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How the value is written; `auto` is in full below 10,000 and compact from there on (1,284 · 12.9K). | `'auto'` | No |
| `prefix` | `string` | Text before the value, in the same style, such as a currency symbol. | — | No |
| `suffix` | `string` | A unit after the value, smaller and in the secondary text color, such as "items" or "ms". | — | No |
| `delta` | `StatisticDelta` | The change compared with an earlier period: `{ value, period, format?, goodWhen? }`. It is shown with an arrow and a sign (+12.5%), never by color alone; its color is the success color when the change is good, the danger color when it is bad, and the secondary text color with `goodWhen: 'none'` or no change. | — | No |
| `trend` | `readonly (number \| null)[]` | Recent values, oldest first, drawn as a Sparkline under the value (about 12 points): the history in the de-emphasis color, the current value as an accent dot. | — | No |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Shows a skeleton in place of the value (and of the change and trend, when given) while the data loads; the size does not change when the data arrives. | — | No |
| `size` | `'md' \| 'lg'` | Size of the value: `md` (24 px) for KPI rows, `lg` (32 px) for the main figure of an area. | `'md'` | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### ValueFormat

How a value is written.
- `'auto'`: in full below 10,000, compact from 10,000 on (1,284 · 12.9K · 4.2M).
- `'number'`: always in full, with grouping separators.
- `'compact'`: always compact.
- `'percent'`: the value is a ratio (0.125 → 12.5%).
- a function: your own formatting (units, currencies).

```ts
type ValueFormat = 'auto' | 'number' | 'compact' | 'percent' | ((value: number) => string)
```

### StatisticDelta

The change of a Statistic compared with an earlier period.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | The change. With the default `format` it is a ratio: 0.125 is shown as +12.5%. | — | Yes |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How the change is written. A function receives the absolute value of the change; the sign and the arrow are added. | `'percent'` | No |
| `period` | `string` | The period it is compared with, such as "vs last month". | — | Yes |
| `goodWhen` | `'up' \| 'down' \| 'none'` | Which direction is good: `up` (revenue), `down` (errors, response time) or `none` (neither, shown in the secondary text color). | `'up'` | No |
